subject: general
question: Who among the following is the head of the 7-member committee set up by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in February 2025 to examine and suggest amendments to the Insurance Act, 1938?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinesh Khara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** constituted a high-level **7-member committee** to review and suggest comprehensive amendments to the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The committee is chaired by **Dinesh Khara**, who is the **former Chairman of the State Bank of India (SBI)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Dinesh Khara.***
 
• The primary objective of this panel is to modernize the legal framework governing the insurance sector to align with the government's vision of **"Insurance for All by 2047"**.
 
• The committee's mandate includes examining provisions related to **capital requirements**, **solvency margins**, and the potential introduction of **composite insurance licenses**, which would allow a single company to offer both life and general insurance products.
 
• This move is expected to enhance the **ease of doing business**, attract more investment, and increase **insurance penetration** across the country by removing outdated regulatory hurdles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**:
 
 
• It is the **statutory body** responsible for regulating and promoting the insurance and re-insurance industries in India.
 
• It was established in **1999** following the recommendations of the **Malhotra Committee** report.
 
• The headquarters of **IRDAI** is located in **Hyderabad**, Telangana, and its current **Chairman** is **Debasish Panda**.
 
 
 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938**:
 
 
• This is the fundamental law that provides the framework for the **regulation** of the insurance business in India.
 
• Major amendments were made in **2015** and **2021**; the latter notably increased the **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** limit in the insurance sector from **49% to 74%**.
 
 
 
• **Dinesh Khara**:
 
 
• He served as the **Chairman of the State Bank of India** from **October 2020** until **August 2024**.
 
• Under his leadership, **SBI** achieved significant milestones in **digital banking** and **profitability**, making his expertise vital for the structural reform of the insurance sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Analysis**:
 
 
• **Swaminathan Janakiraman**: He is currently a **Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and previously served as a Managing Director at **SBI**.
 
• **Ajay Tyagi**: He is a former **Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**, having served from **2017 to 2022**.
 
• **TS Vijayan**: He is a former **Chairman** of both the **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)** and the **IRDAI**.
 
 
 
• **Composite Licensing**: This is a major reform being discussed by the **Dinesh Khara committee**. Currently, Indian law requires separate entities for life, general, and health insurance. A **composite license** would allow insurers to offer multiple types of insurance under one roof, improving **operational efficiency**.
 
• **Insurance Penetration in India**: As of **2024**, India's insurance penetration remains around **4% of its GDP**, which is lower than the global average. The **2025 committee** aims to address this gap by making insurance more accessible and affordable.
</ul
